text:
$HeOrShe glances at a secondary display, checking your $shipOrFleet ID.

"Charity may be a virtue, spacer," $heOrShe says, "but I'd only even consider your request if you were actually in need - and commissioned in service of the Church of Galactic Redemption."

"Mind you that greed is a vice, so pray on that as you move along."
"Hmm," the $post looks over a secondary display, casually tapping through a few reports.
"Hmm," the $post looks over a secondary display, casually tapping through a few reports.

The $post gives you a strange look, then glances at a secondary display. Then, looking slightly alarmed, back at you.

"Wait, are you-" $HisOrHer eyes dart to the display. "You're $playerName! Get yourself off of my comm-link."

$HeOrShe mashes at the cut-off button.
notes: # don't actually flip the first-time flag 'cause player didn't get the essential game info out of this

text: Something comes up, $hisOrHer eyes narrow, expression growing harder. More tapping. Then $heOrShe turns to you, frowning.

Something comes up, $hisOrHer eyes narrow, expression growing harder. More tapping. Then $heOrShe turns to you, frowning.

"You don't become the $post without having seen a few tricks over the cycles. I just didn't expect a captain bearing a $faction commission to attempt the old cargo dump on me."

$HeOrShe sighs, shaking his or her head. "I'm flagging your commission ID for a cycle. Now get off my comms."

"I'm a $post for the Hegemony, not some two-credit League world. I've seen the old dump-the-cargo done by an upstart who thinks they're more clever than the system before, and I will again. You should be hauled before a court martial. But lucky you, I've got enough paperwork, so I'm going to pretend this was one big, stupid mistake."

$HeOrShe sighs, shaking his or her head. "I'm flagging your commission ID for a cycle. Now get off my comms."

"I see your trick, captain, and while I admire your drive to maximize profit, I cannot respect that you're too incompetent to dump your supplies further afield before requesting assistance. You understand that if I was found misappropriating Tri-Tachyon property, they'd bond me into debt-service? I've got wealth, but not much. It'd be life."

$HeOrShe sighs, shaking his or her head. "I'm flagging your commission ID for a cycle. Now get off my comms."

"I may walk with Ludd, but you don't become the $post by taking every spacer's word on faith alone. I'd hoped a captain commissioned by the Church would never attempt a cargo dump scam on me, but here you are."

$HeOrShe sighs, shaking his or her head. "I'm flagging your commission for a cycle, that you might reflect and pray for forgiveness. Now remove your sinning face from my comms."

"I'm no gens-get, captain; I earned my position by serving from Laicaille to Salamanca and I didn't become $post because I'm a fool. I just didn't expect a League captain to attempt the old smuggler's dump on me."

$HeOrShe sighs, shaking his or her head. "I'm flagging your commission ID for a cycle. Now get off my comms."

"You don't become the $post here without knowing a few tricks employed by terrorists and smugglers. I'd have expected if you'd pledged to the Sindrian Diktat you'd know better than to attempt the old cargo dump scam. Stars beyond, you'd get us both sent to Cruor!"

$HeOrShe sighs, shaking his or her head. "I'm flagging your commission ID for a cycle. You'd best hope the Spider doesn't take an interest. Now get off my comms."

"Hmm. Your $shipOrFleet is in decent shape, but your readiness has suffered. Seeing as how you bear a $faction commission, it looks like I might be able to justify providing you with assistance."

$HeOrShe gives you a severe look. "Are you sure you want to call this in now? A commissioned captain is only authorized to receive emergency supplies once per cycle."
options:
bqfs_receiveSupplies:"I need supplies. Badly."
bqfs_receiveSuppliesAbort:"No, I'll do without."

text: The $post simply nods.
"It looks like your $shipOrFleet has taken some hits. Seeing as how you bear a $faction commission, it looks like I can justify providing you with assistance."
"Your $shipOrFleet has taken some serious damage. You have a $faction commission and this is a clear case of need, so I shall provide you with emergency supplies."

"Looks like you've got a handle on your $shipOrFleet's upkeep. I'll not give supplies away for them to end up on the black market."

$HeOrShe holds up one rough hand, "Not accusing you, captain. It's simply a matter of policy that I must justify any emergency supply transfer. If I can't prove they're used to serve $faction interests, then I have to answer for the expense."

$HeOrShe back looks to you, perplexed. "You own your own planet and you've come to me begging for supplies?"

"I'll count this as a joke in poor taste, $playerSirOrMadam."

$HeOrShe doesn't look amused, and doesn't manage to imbue $hisOrHer words with quite the tone of respect $hisOrHer words alone would imply.

script:
$player.unsf_argo_shady_greet = true
SetTextHighlights "unaffiliated"
ShowPersonVisual
UNSFCMD startMission
Call $global.unsf_argonauts updateData
text:
An avatar of a $ManOrWoman appears on the screen "Hey $player.firstName, a spacer like you has just the," $heOrShe pauses, trying to come up with a word, "reputation, i'm looking for."

"I'm $name, and a friend of mine is in need of assistance from an unaffiliated third party fleet." That would be you. "It's vital that the fleet in question is only interested in our, or their own, success." You feel like $heOrShe's done some research on who you are, for better or worse.
options: unsfShadyShuttle:I guess I've been around here and there.

text: The $ManOrWoman gives you a relieved look, "Glad to see you back."

$unsf_argo_shadyName nods down to her TriPad, "The information is rather sensitive, so I would prefer if we talked in person."
As $heOrShe sends over coordinates on $entity.name for your meeting, you ponder if the trouble $HisOrHer 'friend' got into is worth your time.
options:
unsfShadyMeet1:Take a shuttle down to meet Shady
cutCommLinkPolite:"Not right now." [Cut the comm link]
unsfShadyRefuse:"I'm not interested" [Terminate quest]

text:
A disappointed look washes over $HisOrHer face, "Hm, looks like it's back to doing business with pirate-salvagers..."
Without any more hesitation, the avatar dissapears.

The station is so much bigger than it looks from deep space. Despite its intended use as a space vessel, it's surprisingly uncramped, which adds to it's 'planetary city' feel. You walk with several bodyguards through many corridors, hallways, teleporters, all designed for civilian use. You use one and find yourself at a loading dock. $unsf_argo_shadyName should be around here.

The crowd isn't particularly dense, and you're able to discern the people who care about being seen. A $unsf_argo_shadySex stares at you a bit longer than others, and after glancing back, you realise $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe's the one you've been looking for.

The $unsf_argo_shadySex looks over the shoulders of you and your bodyguards, "Might as well 've brought an army at this point," $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe rolls her eyes "I swear, if I get in trouble for this..."

$unsf_argo_shadyName realizes yelling at you will just draw more attention. "Anyway," $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe exhales...

"One of my long-time friends does research for an UNSF engineering company that collaborates with TriTach. Recently, they've started working on a new engine prototype, that uses accelerated particle-antiparticle pairs to cause an energy-dense fissi-" $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe stumbles on $unsf_argo_shadyHisOrHer works, "or was it fusion-" then shrugs briefly.

As you can see, $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe rehearsed at least some of it. "Anyway, this engine would be able to warp a ship into hyperspace from any point in regular space."
options: unsfShadyMeet4:"So a warp drive? Like the kind that brought you here?"

text: "Similar," $unsf_argo_shadyName nods, "although a bit limited and on a much smaller scale. Opening the wormhole would consume a lot of AM fuel, but in turn, let a fleet enter and exit any system freely!"

options: unsfShadyMeet5:"That sounds similar to a Transverse Jump I can do!"
unsfShadyMeet5:"Doesn't that give any fleet using it a huge tactical advantage?"

text:
"That it does!" $unsf_argo_shadyName looks somewhat surprised of your experience with the subject matter, "But it has a lot more uses, past the dreams of an ordinary salvager."

"Understanding the rules that govern this universe's cross-dimensional transit might let us escape the madness that's come over this sector, or better yet", $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe pauses, you can almost see a smirk form on $unsf_argo_shadyHisOrHer face, "travel back home."

It's unclear whether $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe actually believes this specific project is capable of that...
options: unsfShadyMeet6:"Sounds like something worth looking into."

Call $global.unsf_argonauts showMap "Target: $unsf_argo_baseName"

text:
"Funny," $unsf_argo_shadyHeOrShe softly grins, "I said the same thing the first time I heard of it."

"Last $unsf_argo_sciHeOrShe checked in, $unsf_argo_sciName was $unsf_argo_baseOnOrAt $unsf_argo_baseName, about $unsf_argo_baseDist ly away. Head there, provide the assistance she requested, and report back."

$unsf_argo_shadyName gives you a disappointed look, "I'm not able to provide you any compensation for what's to come, but I do have some fuel you may use for your journey!"

She waves you goodbye as you part ways "Godspeed, $player.firstName!"
*Scientist says hi and asks if you were the one Shady sent*
*Scientist gives you directions to constellation with abandoned station*

Your $shipOrFleet approaches the abandoned station.

The structure resembles a Tri-Tachyon research facility, with what seem like additional modules attached over time.

Salvor teams cut through fused locks and infiltrate the station. Most of the bulkheads seem stable enough to support an atmosphere, yet the station seems to have been depressurized on purpose.

It's evident that whoever left this place, did so in a hurry, and rather than destroying the research in question, just made it tedious to get to.

You watch as one of the teams makes it to the research lab of interest. They see the eerily familiar AI core sockets, cyber-interface chambers, and data cores... lots of them.

Seems like a lot of data was collected, but on what? And for what purpose? "It'll take us a while to analyze these, boss. From the looks of it, about a forth of the data is encrypted, and another fourth is straight up gone!"
options: unsfStationExplore3:How much time will it take?

text: "10, maybe 12 hours, a while." The tech tries to put it in the best way possible. "Usually we'd just take these and scan them after, but disconnecting these out of order may corrupt the rest of the data."

options:
unsfStationExplore5Wait:Find something to do for the rest of the day.
unsfStationExplore5UseAI:Plug in a semi-intelligent AI core to help with data mining.

script:
SetEnabled unsfStationExplore5NoAI false
SetTooltip unsfStationExplore5NoAI "Requires a beta-level AI core."
options:
unsfStationExplore5Wait:Find something to do for the rest of the day.
unsfStationExplore5UseAI:Plug in a semi-intelligent AI core to help with data mining.

text: The next several hours are as tense as they are boring. You wait for your tech officer to give the all clear, while keeping watch on the sensors for unwanted guests. After what feels like a cycle of trying to keep your eyes open, his voice finally comes through. "I think we got everything, heading back now!"

Making use of the AI interface sockets, you bring in a beta core to help the techs crack this data repository. It's smart enough to fill in the gaps and run decryption algorithms, but doesn't care nearly enough to sabotage or relay the data in question.

The whole mess is sorted before the hour is up, and the AI core is placed back into your holding cell.
